one_liner: AI civic letters for constituents: prove paid demand and gov-email delivery before scaling.
oneLiner: AI civic letters for constituents: prove paid demand and gov-email delivery before scaling.
directive: Use BUSINESS.md as the current EIR seed plan; operator merge is required before authority upgrades. Resolve dispatch/project-id mismatch before pitching externally.
authority: POM soul-review + wrk.dog merge constitute adoption - operator ruling 2026-06-12; see the PR's POM record

methods: Read prior planning artifacts and master plan.
Inspected implemented API, worker, payment, delivery, moderation, officials, and Prisma surfaces.
Used repo files as evidence and labeled external market claims as assumptions.
Recorded the dispatch/project-id mismatch as a surprise spike.

planningMethod: EIR genesis upgrade from repository evidence, bottom-up market model, reconciled unit economics, and validation-gated roadmap.

customer.primary: U.S. resident with a concrete civic concern, desired outcome, and ZIP code.
segments: Residents with local service, zoning, transit, school, enforcement, or policy concerns.
Future organizations such as HOAs and nonprofits, explicitly out of launch scope.
customer.pain: They do not know the right official, applicable law, formal framing, or delivery path.

market.method: Bottom-up from metro reach, annual paid incidence, repeat issues, and average package price.
market.beachheadSOM: USD 120,000/year [assumption: 3 metros x 250,000 households x 1.0 percent x USD 16]
market.initialSAM: USD 2,025,000/year [assumption: 25 metros x 300,000 households x 1.5 percent x USD 18]
market.consumerTAMProxy: USD 18,000,000/year [assumption: 100 metros x 500,000 households x 1.0 percent x 2 issues x USD 18]
market.caveat: Consumer-only market may be too small unless repeat use or organization/API revenue validates.

futureStreams: Human-reviewed complex sends [assumption: packaging still unvalidated]
Organization/API access [assumption: future wedge, not launch scope]

revenueAssumptions: USD 15 launch ARPP [assumption: 25 percent single, 50 percent three-pack, 25 percent full-spread]
Launch year revenue USD 34,560 [assumption: 180 monthly paid submissions x USD 16 x 12 months]
Expansion year revenue USD 600,000 [assumption: 2,500 monthly paid submissions x USD 20 x 12 months]
costAssumptions: COGS plus Stripe equals 12 percent of revenue [evidence: MASTER_PLAN.md]
Fixed platform starts near USD 200/month [evidence: MASTER_PLAN.md]
Local official data may add USD 100 to USD 500/month [evidence: .planning/PROJECT.md]
sensitivityTests: If conversion is 1 percent instead of 3 percent, revenue falls by about 67 percent [assumption: funnel math].
If COGS plus payment fees are 25 percent instead of 12 percent, launch-year EBITDA falls by USD 4,493 [assumption: model delta].
If local data costs USD 500/month instead of USD 250/month, annual fixed cost rises by USD 3,000 [assumption: provider-cost delta].

alternatives: LegalZoom or attorney help for formal legal documents.

holes.hole: Users may not pay for something they can do manually or through free tools.
holes.residualRisk: High until real paid cohorts exist.

holes.hole: Government-email deliverability may make the core promise unreliable.
holes.mitigation: SPF/DKIM/DMARC, Postmark, bounce thresholds, and domain monitoring.
holes.residualRisk: High because inbox placement is externally controlled.

holes.hole: Citation errors could damage trust and create legal-adjacent risk.
holes.mitigation: Search-bound research and citation verification before drafting.
holes.residualRisk: Medium because source coverage can still be incomplete.

holes.hole: Consumer-only market may be too small for venture returns.
holes.mitigation: Treat organization/API revenue as a separate validation gate.

strategy: Prove paid consumer demand and delivery reliability in narrow metros before adding community, coalition, certified mail, or organization features.

goToMarket.firstCustomers: First 100 customers from operator distribution, local civic threads, neighborhood newsletters, and issue-specific search pages [assumption].
channels: Long-tail SEO from opt-in public civic records [evidence: .planning/GENESIS.md]
doNotDoYet: Organization/API sales before consumer delivery is stable.

operatorWorkflow.daily: Review flagged submissions, bounces, spam complaints, failed jobs, and treasury reconciliation.
operatorWorkflow.weekly: Review conversion, coverage, delivery, chargeback, and margin gates.
operatorWorkflow.escalation: Stop new feature work after repeated gate misses and diagnose the failing gate.

constraints: Workspace-only plan; no external market research performed.
Civic content is politically sensitive and must avoid harassment, defamation, and legal-advice posture.
Launch uses fixed Stripe tiers in the repo, not dynamic pricing.
Official-data source choice remains an open spike.
Registry says watchlist / personal research asset, not near-term investible BOS until operator confirmation.
Dispatch project id and repo name do not match the CivicState workspace content.

rules: Researcher may only cite provided source results.
Drafter includes AI disclosure, disclaimer, and CAN-SPAM footer.
Moderation blocks threats and flags risky submissions.

unknowns: Whether the registry should point this dispatch to CivicState or a different Brooks History asset.

assumptionLedger.claim: COGS plus Stripe equals 12 percent of revenue.
One operator can manage launch exceptions.
WrkPlug shared rails lower infra and CAC.
assumptionLedger.test: Operator adoption decision and migration estimate.

versionHistory.change: EIR genesis soul created from repo evidence after scrutiny gaps.

roadmapGate.next: Operator/POM review, registry mismatch resolution, then beta validation instrumentation and official-data spike.
